newsitem.title: USA: ProxyMed to buy Walgreen electronic network.
newsitem.headline: ProxyMed to buy Walgreen electronic network.

text.p: Walgreen Co agreed to sell its electronic prescription network, Pre-Scribe, to ProxyMed Inc, both companies said Monday.
The Pre-Scribe network allows prescriptions to be filled through a direct electronic link between physicians' computers and local pharmacies.
Pre-Scribe had been operated previously by Integrated Systems Solutions Corp, a division of IBM Corp.
ProxyMed is acquiring copyrights, trademarks, and software relating to Pre-Scribe. Currently, several thousand physicians across the country are using Pre-Scribe.

Under a second agreement, ProxyMed will provide connectivity between Walgreen pharmacies and ProxyMed's physician network ProxyNet for 12 years, of which the first three are on an exclusive basis. Walgreen will pay a per transaction fee for each prescription processed through both Pre-Scribe and ProxyNet.

ProxyMed is currently developing connectivity to 150,000 physicians through agreements with 27 physician practice management companies, integrating electronic prescription modules into the physician's existing software.

Walgreen is the nation's largest drugstore chain with 1996 sales of $11.8 billion. The company filled 190 million prescriptions in 1996, more than eight percent of the retail market. Walgreen has nearly 2,300 stores nationwide and plans to operate 3,000 stores by the year 2000.
ProxyMed is a healthcare information technology company that provides on-line clinical services to physicians.
